chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hajjaj) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a slave girl was bought for him from Kufa. He said: She went to attend to some need, and she called out, 'O my mother.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to her, 'Do you have a mother?' She said, 'Yes.' So he ordered that she be returned (to her owner/mother), and he said, 'I did not want it if I kept her that I would see in my children what I dislike (i.e., separation from their mother).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping a slave girl who has a living mother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and emotional intelligence in manumission, extending the concept of family preservation beyond mere legal ownership. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the psychological bond between mother and child is a significant factor in human dignity, influencing the decision to free a slave not just for piety, but to prevent potential familial disruption. This narrative serves as a practical precedent for valuing the maternal relationship in Islamic jurisprudence and social ethics.
